BASIC · AI AGENT
An AI agent is an LLM that can act
Give it a goal. It thinks, uses a tool, looks at the result, and repeats until the goal is done.
Goal
1. Think and plan
2. Act with a tool
3. Observe result
Repeat until the goal is done
Brain
The LLM reasons and decides the next step.
Hands
Tools: search, APIs, databases, code, email.
Memory
Remembers the goal, past steps and results.
5
BASIC · AGENTIC AI
From GenAI to agents to agentic AI
1
Generative AI
Answers a prompt with new content. One question in, one answer out.
“Draft a refund email.”
2
AI agent
Uses tools in a loop to complete one task by itself.
“Check the order and send the refund email.”
3
Agentic AI
A goal-driven system that plans, splits work between agents, remembers and adapts.
“Run the whole refund process.”
More autonomy at every step: the AI decides more, the human supervises less.

BASIC · AI SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
An AI system is five layers
1. Users and apps
Chat window, web app, mobile app, voice
2. Backend and API
Login, limits, request handling
3. Orchestration
Prompt templates, memory, routing, guardrails
4. Models and tools
The LLM, retriever, external APIs, code runner
5. Data and compute
Documents, vector store, databases, GPUs
The request travels down the layers. The answer travels back up.

FOUNDATIONS · LLM
An LLM predicts the next token
A Large Language Model is trained on huge amounts of text, so it can understand and generate human-like language.
1. Your text is split into tokens (illustrative split)
Hello
,
how
are
you
?
2. The model picks the most likely next token, again and again
The
capital
of
France
is

8
INSIDE AN LLM · THE PIPELINE
From your text to the next word, in six steps
1
Tokenize
Split text into pieces.
The | cat | sat
2
Token IDs
Each piece becomes a number.
464 | 3797 | 3332
3
Embed
Each ID becomes a vector.
[0.12, -0.48, 0.91 …]
4
Transformer layers
Attention and feed-forward maths, repeated many times.
5
Scores
One score for every word in the vocabulary.
6
Softmax and pick
Scores become probabilities. The next token is chosen.
… sat on
Numbers shown are illustrative. Real models use vocabularies of tens of thousands of tokens.
9
INSIDE AN LLM · EMBEDDINGS
Words become lists of numbers
cheque
cheque book
banana
Each square is one number. Darker means a bigger value. Illustrative.
Similar meaning
Similar numbers. “cheque” and “cheque book” look alike.
Different meaning
Different numbers. “banana” looks nothing like them.
Why it matters
Computers cannot read words, but they can compare numbers. This powers search and RAG.

INSIDE AN LLM · TRANSFORMER
One transformer block, repeated
Input embeddings + word position
Multi-head self-attention
Add and normalise
Feed-forward network
Add and normalise
× N layers (dozens in big models)
Scores → softmax → next word
Attention
Mixes information between words.
Feed-forward
Processes each word’s numbers on its own.
Add and normalise
Keeps the numbers stable as they pass through many layers.
The core operation
Mostly matrix multiplication: big grids of numbers multiplied together.
12
INSIDE AN LLM · THE REAL CALCULATION
Scores become probabilities, temperature included
For “The cat sat on the ___” the model scores each word: mat 2.0, floor 1.0, moon 0.1. Softmax turns each score into e to the power of (score ÷ temperature), then divides by the total.
Temperature 0.5
Focused
mat 86.4%
floor 11.7%
moon 1.9%
Temperature 1.0
Balanced
mat 65.9%
floor 24.2%
moon 9.9%
Temperature 1.5
Creative
mat 55.7%
floor 28.6%
moon 15.7%
Low temperature sharpens the winner. High temperature flattens the odds, so unlikely words get picked more often.

INSIDE AN LLM · TRAINING
How an LLM learns
Read text: books, web, code
Predict the next token
Compare with the real one
Adjust the weights
Repeat billions of times
Pre-training
Learns language and facts by predicting the next token.
Fine-tuning
Learns to follow instructions and answer in a useful format.
Human feedback
Learns which answers people prefer: helpful, safe, clear.

FOUNDATIONS · PROMPTS
System prompt vs user prompt
SYSTEM PROMPT
How should I behave?
You are a banking assistant. Be professional. Never expose confidential data.
USER PROMPT
What should I do?
I want to apply for a new cheque book.
Prompt template
One reusable prompt with variables. 1,000 documents need one template, not 1,000 prompts.
Extract the details from: {document}
15
FOUNDATIONS · CONTROLS
Temperature and max_tokens
Temperature sets how varied the answer is. max_tokens sets how long it can be.
0
Deterministic
Extraction, SQL, classification
0.2–0.4
Focused
Documents, banking agents
0.5–0.7
Balanced
Chat, general answers
0.8–1.0
Creative
Ideas, stories, variety
max_tokens
The maximum output length. max_tokens=500 stops the answer at about 500 tokens.
Good to know
temperature=0 is the most predictable setting, but not a guarantee of identical output every call.
16
FOUNDATIONS · CONTEXT WINDOW
The context window is the model’s working memory
Everything the model reads and writes has to fit inside it at one time.
Small window: only a little fits
System
Question
Answer
Large window: whole documents fit
System
Chat history
Long document or code
Answer
Too much text does not fit. That is why large documents are split into chunks and only the relevant ones are sent to the model.

INTERMEDIATE · WHY TOOLS
An LLM alone can think, not do
It can reason and write an answer. But on its own it has gaps:
No real-time data
Unreliable at calculations
Cannot call APIs or reach your data
Cannot act: send email, book, run code
Tools turn thinking into doing
From your notes: what an LLM cannot do alone
18
INTERMEDIATE · TOOLS
Bind, call, execute
1
Tool binding
Give the tools to the LLM so it knows what exists and what each does.
2
Tool calling
The LLM chooses a tool and suggests its arguments. It does not run it.
3
Tool execution
Our code runs the tool and sends the result back to the LLM.
Example: “What is the weather in Pune?”
User asks
LLM suggests get_weather(“Pune”)
App runs the weather API
LLM writes the answer
19
INTERMEDIATE · TOOL CALLING AS A SEQUENCE
Who talks to whom, in order
User
Your app
LLM
Tool / API
1. “Where is my order?”
2. prompt + tool list
3. suggests get_order(1042)
4. your app runs the tool
5. result: shipped, arrives Friday
6. result goes back to the LLM
7. final answer, sent to the user

INTERMEDIATE · RAG
RAG hands the model your data at question time
The problem
The model has never seen your private documents, and may guess when it does not know.
The fix
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: find the relevant pieces first, then let the model answer from them. Like an open-book exam.
Question
Retriever
Relevant chunks
LLM
Grounded answer

INTERMEDIATE · RAG STEP 1
Index: turn documents into searchable vectors
From your notes: PDF to Vector Store
Load and split
Read the PDF, cut it into chunks.
Embed
Turn each chunk into numbers.
Store
Save vectors in a vector store.
Done once, ahead of time. After this the documents can be searched by meaning.
22
INTERMEDIATE · RAG STEP 2
Retrieve: find the chunks that match the question
From your notes: the retriever flow
1. Embed the query
Same model, same kind of vector.
2. Search
The retriever finds the nearest chunks.
3. Prompt the LLM
Chunks plus query become the prompt.

INTERMEDIATE · FULL RAG ARCHITECTURE
Two pipelines share one vector database
A. INGESTION (offline, done once)
Documents
Loader
Text splitter
Embedding model
Vector database
B. QUERY (online, every question)
Question
Embed question
Search top-k
Rerank
Prompt + chunks
LLM answer
The amber boxes are the same database: ingestion writes to it, and every question searches it. A reranker re-orders the top results so the best chunks reach the LLM.

Text splitter

Chunk 3

ADVANCED · FULL AI AGENT ARCHITECTURE
The complete agent, in one picture
1. Context builder
Gathers the goal and the right memories into a prompt.
2. LLM and planner
Reasons, splits the goal into steps and picks an action.
3. Harness
Runs tools safely: permissions, retries, logging, limits.
4. Observation
Results flow back, and the loop repeats.
REASON → ACT → OBSERVE → REFLECT → REPEAT

ADVANCED · AGENT MEMORY
The three kinds of agent memory
Agent core (LLM)
Short-term memory
The current conversation inside the context window. Gone when the session ends.
Working memory
Scratchpad for the current task: variables, plan, intermediate results.
Long-term memory (vector database)
Episodic: past events
Semantic: facts, preferences
Procedural: how-to skills

ADVANCED · THE REACT PATTERN
ReAct: reason, act, observe
Thought: what do I need?
Action: call a tool
Observation: read the result
Repeat, then give the final answer
Thought: I need the order status. Action: get_order(1042) Observation: shipped, arrives Friday Thought: I can answer now. Final: Your order ships Friday.
ReAct combines Reasoning and Acting. The written thoughts help the model plan, and the observations keep it grounded in real results.
31
ADVANCED · AGENT LOOP IN ACTION
One agent, step by step
Goal: “Book the cheapest flight to Delhi on Friday.”
Step
Agent thinks
Action and result
1
I need the flight options for Friday.
Tool: search_flights(“Delhi”, Friday). Returns 3 flights.
2
Compare prices and pick the cheapest.
Reasoning only. No tool needed.
3
Book that flight.
Tool: book_flight(id). Returns a confirmation.
4
Goal reached. Report back.
Final answer: flight booked, with the details.

LLM

JSON-RPC messages
MCP servers
Files server

Real systems
Documents
Databases
SaaS apps

ADVANCED · LANGCHAIN RUNNABLES
Runnables: small steps you can chain
Sequence
Run one after another; output feeds the next.
chain = prompt | llm | parser
Parallel
Run side by side; results are combined.
RunnableParallel(summary=a, translation=b)
Lambda
Turn your own Python function into a step.
RunnableLambda(add_name)
Passthrough
Pass the input forward without changing it.
RunnablePassthrough()

Key takeaways
GenAI
Creates new text, images, code and audio.
LLM
Predicts the next token, one at a time.
Tools and RAG
Let the model act and use your own data.
AI agent
LLM plus tools plus memory, in a loop.
Agentic AI
Agents that plan, delegate, remember and adapt to finish a whole goal.
